related_questions.question: What to do immediately after testing positive for COVID?
related_questions.snippet: If your COVID-19 test is positive Monitor your symptoms. If you have any emergency warning signs, seek emergency care immediately. Seek health care right away for treatment if you have risk factors for severe illness. Treatment may be an option to make your symptoms less severe and shorten the time you are sick.

related_questions.question: Am I still contagious after 5 days of testing positive for COVID?
related_questions.snippet: “A big study came out in the fall of 2023 which showed that most people are the most contagious on day four of symptoms with COVID and then it wanes from there,” said Dr. Roberts. While people become less contagious over time, they are still contagious with COVID for an average of eight days.

related_questions.question: What do I do if I've been exposed to someone who tested positive for COVID-19?

text_blocks.snippet: If you've been exposed to someone who tested positive for COVID-19, you should immediately start taking precautions, including wearing a high-quality mask, avoiding places where you can't wear a mask, and taking extra precautions around vulnerable individuals. You should also get tested at least 5 days after your last exposure, even if you don't have symptoms, and continue taking precautions through day 10.
snippet_highlighted_words: immediately start taking precautions, including wearing a high-quality mask, avoiding places where you can't wear a mask, and taking extra precautions around vulnerable individuals

list.snippet: Start Precautions Immediately: Begin taking precautions right away, even before you get tested.
High-Quality Mask: Wear a high-quality mask or respirator, such as an N95, whenever you're around others.
Avoid Crowds: Avoid crowded indoor spaces where you can't wear a mask consistently.
Vulnerable Individuals: Be extra careful around people who are more likely to get very sick from COVID-19.
Testing: Get tested for COVID-19 at least 5 full days after your last exposure.
Monitor Symptoms: Watch for any symptoms of COVID-19.
Isolation: If you test positive, isolate yourself at home according to guidance from your healthcare provider or local health department.
